transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... I spend most of my day just going back over the same things in my house. The outlets, the locks on the doors, my tools, even just dust. I keep checking and fixing them, again and again. I do it until I'm completely worn out, but... I still don't feel sure enough to just leave it alone.

When you are checking these things repeatedly, is it because you are trying to prevent a specific, dreaded outcome or harm from happening, or is it more about a need for things to be 'just right' or perfect?

It's definitely about stopping something bad from happening. It's not about things being perfect. 

It's like... even when I know I did the job right, these really ugly thoughts just keep jumping in. I'll get it in my head that a loose wire I missed is going to burn the house down, or... or that a nail I left out somewhere is going to step on and hurt my wife. I try to push the thoughts out, I really do, but they just come right back stronger. That's why I have to keep checking.

When you are performing these checks, do you feel that the act of checking itself is the primary source of your distress, or is the distress primarily coming from the intrusive thoughts about the harm occurring?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about it like that. 

It's kind of... it's all just one big mess. The thoughts are awful, and they start the whole thing, making my chest tight. But then being stuck checking a lock or a wire for an hour when I'm already exhausted... that's miserable, too. I don't really know which one is the main source of the bad feelings. They just sort of bleed together.

When you have these thoughts about a wire starting a fire or your wife getting hurt, do you realize that these thoughts are coming from your own mind, or do you sometimes feel like they are coming from somewhere else?

I know they're my own thoughts. I mean, they're crazy thoughts, and I don't want to have them, but... yeah, I know it's just my own brain doing it. It doesn't feel like someone else is putting them in there or anything like that. It's just my own head working against me.
Do you feel that the amount of time you spend checking these things is excessive or unreasonable, even though you feel compelled to do them?

Yeah, I do. I know it's completely unreasonable. That's actually why I'm here. I spend most of my day just... going back over the same things. The electrical outlets, the locks on the doors, my tools, even just checking for dust in the house. I check them and fix them again and again until I'm just completely worn out. And the worst part is, even after all that time, I still don't feel sure enough to just leave it alone. I know it's excessive, but I just can't stop myself.
